description: Canonical screens, each with its design states. 39 board frames collapse to 14 screens: most frames are STATES of one screen, and modelling them that way is what keeps four implementations aligned. `owner` decides who builds it — `sample` means this repo's sample-ui; `sdk` means the SDK renders it inside its own flow and we must not rebuild it.

The session card at 5:00 is drawn on the new frame itself (5487:1358), so this state no longer needs transposing.
Countdown at 1:40. Not drawn on the new layout.

The 2026-08-13 ruling is kept rather than deleted because it is why the app was built on 5206-4037 at all. The component and its sample_env_chip id survive in components.json and test-ids.json; the environment is a property of the session token now, and the result card is what publishes it. promote the product card's two label runs to composite type styles — both are composed from primitives today (see the cardLabelRuns delta)
a semantic role for Off_black, as a light/dark pair (see the offBlack delta)
a floating elevation role; spec/components.json references elevation.floating and no token defines it (see the floatingElevation delta)

screens.frameOmitsTheAvatar: Neither frame draws the header avatar button and the app KEEPS it (plan §7.5): its absence is a drawing omission, not a removal, and without it the screen has no profile switch at all. sample_profile_avatar_button keeps its target and profiles.yaml keeps working. Recorded here so the next conformance pass does not report it as an extra.
screens.pageBackgroundOpenQuestion: OPEN 2026-08-25. Both frames paint the PAGE with `Card BG` and the nav pill with `Main BG` — the opposite of what those two variables are named for, and the opposite of what the app ships (page color.background, pill color.surface). The separation is the same one step either way, just inverted. The pill cannot move on its own: with the page left as it is, pill and page become the same colour and the bar loses its edge on every tab. Moving the page instead repaints Verifications and Settings, which this frame does not draw. Needs an owner ruling; until then the app keeps its current mapping and PVR-A7 ships without the pill-fill change. See docs/plan/products-visual-refresh-android.md §3.4.
screens.sectionRename: 'Authentication' -> 'Biometric Authentication' (node 5487:1364), and the page subtitle to '...powered by our Anti-Fraud SDKs' (5487:1356).

screens.title: Verifications

states.note: NavBar hidden, selection bar replaces it.

Snackbar with undo; counts drop 11→9. TWO RULES ADDED 2026-08-17 after review. (1) Removing the last row of the ACTIVE filter must fall back to All — otherwise the screen is blank under a chip reading 0 with nothing to explain why, which is what Android shipped. The design has no frame for this because its delete happens from the All filter. (2) Both removal paths, the swipe and the selection bar, must run one shared handler; Android had two copies of the reset and only one would have been fixed.

additions: An empty-list message, which the design does not draw. The app seeds no verification rows — a persisted row claims a job was submitted, and the eleven fixtures never were — so a first launch shows the chips over nothing until a real submission lands. Two texts behind one id: nothing yet, versus nothing matching the active filter.
screens.note: SELECT MODE REPLACES THE BOTTOM CHROME: the selection bar is full-bleed at the bottom with a top border, and the nav bar is NOT behind it (node 5206:2491). The header's trailing action becomes "Cancel". The bar is the screen's state but the shell's slot, so the content inset does not change when one bar replaces the other. The removal confirmation is transient — never saved across navigation, or opening a verification and coming back replays a confirmation you already spent.

screens.title: Verification details
entryPoints: POST-SUBMISSION: the app lands here in the processing state once a job is submitted (observed 202 Accepted straight after the ID form's Continue)
additions: A 'Check status' button stands in for the pull-to-refresh the design draws in the processing state. The gesture itself is deferred with the rest of pull-to-refresh (docs/plan/sample-apps-plan.md 8.1); the button is what makes the real GET /v3/status call reachable in the meantime.
screens.note: The details screen doubles as the result screen, which is why the result card belongs here rather than needing a new home. NO NAV BAR: it is a pushed screen, even though its route lives in the verifications graph. You leave it by going back, not by switching tab. The RESULT CARD and its callback counters are hidden on a release build unless the `probes` launch argument asks for them, and always shown in debug (2026-08-25): the affordance still ships on the release classpath, minified and shrunk, because that is where consumption defects surface — compiling it out with a debug-only source set would also make the argument impossible. The rest of the screen is unchanged either way, so a partner sees the design's screen and automation sees the card.

screens.title: Settings
sections: CAPTURE (two rows: Enhanced SmartSelfie™, Agent mode — mutually exclusive)
SDK SCREENS — SHOW OR SKIP FLOW STEPS

links.licenses: in-app, the licenses screen — not a URL

screens.linkPresentation: Per row, and split on what the destination can render (measured 2026-08-25). ABOUT — Documentation and Support open IN-APP: Custom Tabs on Android (androidx.browser), SFSafariViewController on iOS, url_launcher inAppBrowserView on Flutter, expo-web-browser on React Native. A WebView is deliberately NOT the pattern on any platform: the page would lose the user's session, autofill and password manager, and this is code partners copy. LEGAL — Terms of Service and Privacy Policy EJECT to the system browser, because both pages serve their document as an embedded PDF (a Webflow CDN asset, hash in the filename) and a mobile browser renders an embedded PDF as a stub with an Open button rather than the document; framing that inside the app makes the app look like it failed. The canonical page URLs stay as they are — linking the CDN asset directly would show the document but hard-codes a path that changes on every re-upload, and the same canonical URL is what the SDK consent screen uses. The in-app toolbar takes a colour PER SCHEME from the design tokens (primary in light, surface in dark); one shared colour left a white bar on a white page. Android warms the browser while Settings is open but does NOT pre-fetch: speculatively downloading a 649 KB docs page on a partner's mobile data is the wrong trade.
screens.note: The PROFILE row opens the profiles LIST, not the active profile's own page — configuring any profile and creating one are both reached from there. Its avatar takes the ACTIVE profile's hue from design-tokens.json profileHues, indexed by list position, so the summary, the list and the products header never draw the same profile in three colours. The ENVIRONMENT section was removed on 2026-08-24: it was never in the design, and it existed only because the sandbox launch argument was an override rather than a source. Both are gone — the token's api_url decides the environment, and a run reports it on sample_result_environment. The three SDK-step switches include or omit their screen (see components.json settingsToSdkMapping), and the CONSENT row carries one overridden supporting line: when the linked token binds consent it reads 'The token grants consent, so the screen is skipped', because a switch reading ON while the token has taken the decision away is a lie the screen tells. The switch stays live — it still decides the next run made without a bound token. The DEBUG section holding the Scenarios row renders on debug builds only (see drawerPresentation): the screen takes it as a nullable slot the host fills, because sample-ui runs under eight identities and may not read a host's BuildConfig.

screens.title: Profiles
screens.note: Creating a profile does NOT make it active: the confirmation carries the offer. The created state shows a toast reading "<organisation> created" with action "Make active", placed 24 above the safe area — the host already insets a pushed route past the system bar, so adding that inset again lifts the toast into the list. Each row's avatar hue is its position in the list, cycled.

screens.title: Profile configuration
screens.note: USER DETAILS — ATTACHED TO EVERY JOB. This is the per-profile default that seeds the userDetails screen. The app bar title is the PROFILE'S NAME. The CTA has two states: on any other profile it reads "Make this profile active" and both saves and activates; on the profile that is already active it is DISABLED and reads "Active profile". Screen spacing is 14 between the header, the section label, the card and the CTA — not the 8 used inside a card.

screens.title: New profile
screens.note: A profile name, then the four user details that will live under it, each field carrying a 17 leading icon; the CTA "Create profile" stays disabled until name, first name and last name are present, and all four details are stored as the new profile's defaults. The sheet must open at its CONTENT height rather than the platform's half-height partial state: at half height the fifth field clips and the CTA sits below the fold.

screens.title: Scan token

states.note: No design node: the expiry gate can send a partner here mid-journey, and the caption is replaced by why they were moved so a scanner nobody asked for is not a dead tap. The sentence belongs to the shared UI rather than a host, so the four apps cannot word it differently.

screens.note: Camera QR scan for linking a token session. The reticle frame is hidden in the design in favour of the scan glyph; a manual-entry row with Paste and a 'Simulate a successful scan' affordance are both present — the simulate row is what makes this screen testable without a QR source.

screens.title: Open-source licenses

states.note: NO DESIGN FRAME: the design set has a LEGAL row called 'Open-source licenses' and no destination for it. Built from components this app already has — TopAppBar, SectionLabel, SettingRow — so it cannot look bolted on, and deliberately as a flat list rather than the rounded section cards the other screens use: two hundred rows inside one card compose all of them at once.
The notices are generated into the binary at build time, so an empty list means the asset did not ship. It says that rather than showing nothing.

screens.note: Two sections, because not every dependency is open source: 'OPEN-SOURCE COMPONENTS' lists each artifact with its declared licence and expands to the full licence text, and 'UNDER GOOGLE'S OWN TERMS' lists the ML Kit, Play Integrity and Android SDK artifacts, which declare terms-of-service pages rather than a licence — there is no text to ship for those, so the row opens the page. Content comes from scripts/generate_licenses.py, which resolves the RELEASE runtime classpath (the SDK's transitive set plus the app's own, which is what a partner ships), walks parent POMs, keeps more than one licence per artifact, and FAILS the build rather than emitting 'Unknown'. The first-party SDK is excluded: a partner licenses it from Smile ID, so its terms are not a third-party notice. Every platform generates its own file — the classpath differs per platform — and no port hand-maintains a list.

screens.title: Scenario drawer
screens.note: A debug affordance, not a designed screen. AGENTS.md mandates it; the design does not cover it.

openQuestions.question: The chosen products layout (board 01b, expressive grid) has ONE state. The token-session, token-expired and production states exist only on the superseded list layout (boards 01 and 07). Should those states be re-drawn on the grid layout, or may engineering transpose the session card / env chip / token ring onto it?
openQuestions.recommendation: Engineering transposes; the header, session card and nav bar are unchanged between the two layouts, so only the card grid differs. Confirm rather than assume, since it changes vertical space above the grid.
openQuestions.status: RESOLVED 2026-08-13 — owner ruled the grid is the build target and the prototype will not be updated, so engineering transposes the session card, environment chip and token ring onto the grid. Design may re-draw the states later.

openQuestions.question: The products grid shows 5 job types (SmartSelfie Enrollment, SmartSelfie Auth, Document Verification, Enhanced Doc Verification, Biometric KYC) plus one empty slot. The SDK's JobType enum has 7: EnhancedKyc(5) and BVN(7) are absent. Are those intentionally out of scope for the sample, or does the empty slot belong to one of them?
openQuestions.blocks: final product list; consumption lanes can only exercise what the sample exposes
openQuestions.recommendation: Decide explicitly. Both missing types are form/API-shaped rather than capture-shaped, so leaving them out is defensible — but then the sample never exercises them and no CI lane can.
openQuestions.sdkEvidence: iOS `buildJobRequest()` states the BVN job type is NOT SUPPORTED and throws. Leaving BVN out of the grid is therefore the defensible default; EnhancedKyc remains a genuine product decision.
openQuestions.status: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-13 — RESOLVED: ADD Enhanced KYC (6 products, slot filled). BVN stays out — iOS throws on it. Design ask: one more product card (icon + hue).

openQuestions.question: Board 05 is titled 'Consent & KYC' but contains no consent screen — the consent frames live in board 04 ('Consent & user details'). Rename 05 to 'KYC / ID details' to avoid a wrong-board lookup?
openQuestions.status: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-13 — housekeeping only; ask design to rename board 05 to 'KYC / ID details' when convenient.

openQuestions.question: The Settings footer reads 'Smile ID Sample App · 1.0.0' while the agreed app identity is 'UseSmileID Sample' (spec/app-identity.json). Which string ships?
openQuestions.recommendation: Use the agreed display name in the footer so the app matches its launcher label.
openQuestions.status: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-13 — RESOLVED: 'UseSmileID Sample' everywhere. SUPERSEDED 2026-08-25 (ruled 2026-08-24, 'go with the design'): the footer follows node 5206:2898 and reads 'Smile ID Sample App · 1.0.0'. This does NOT change app-identity.json, whose 'UseSmileID Sample' is the launcher label and store identity, settled against the ids the SDK repos reserve. The footer is brand copy and the launcher label is identity; after this change they legitimately differ, so do not 'fix' one to match the other. sample-ui takes versionLabel as a parameter precisely because the module runs under eight identities.

openQuestions.question: The ABOUT section links 'docs.usesmileid.com'. Confirm that domain is live, or point it at the current documentation host.
openQuestions.status: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-13 — RESOLVED: link to docs.smileidentity.com. CORRECTED 2026-08-25: both hosts are CNAMEs to the same GitBook site and https://docs.smileidentity.com/ answers 307 → https://docs.usesmileid.com/, so the design's own copy is the current one and the spec was carrying the legacy host. The row's supporting line and its URL are both docs.usesmileid.com. The apex domains agree the same way: smileidentity.com 301s to usesmileid.com.

openQuestions.question: Settings CAPTURE has two rows: 'Smile to capture / Passive capture — smile detection' and 'Agent mode'. Agent mode is SelfieCaptureConfig.allowAgentMode. What does 'Smile to capture' set? enableEnhancedLiveness inverted, or something else?
openQuestions.blocks: the CAPTURE section and any flow it configures
openQuestions.recommendation: Get an SDK answer rather than inferring; the two switches must not silently set the same field.
openQuestions.status: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-13 — RESOLVED: ON → enableEnhancedLiveness = false. SUPERSEDED 2026-08-25: node 5206:2898 renames the row to 'Enhanced SmartSelfie™ / Face capture uses head-turns' and draws it ON, so the mapping is direct rather than inverted and the default capture behaviour is the head-turn challenge. The question is answered and closed; the current mapping lives in components.json settingsToSdkMapping and the renamed id in test-ids.json.

openQuestions.question: The design uses soft tinted status pills for all four statuses; the design system's badge tokens are saturated. Add soft variants to the design system, or change the design?
openQuestions.recommendation: Add soft variants to the system — the design applies them consistently across all four roles, so this is a system gap rather than a one-off.
openQuestions.status: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-13 — RESOLVED: keep the design's soft pills; add soft variants to the design system.

openQuestions.question: The ID-details form is only drawn for Biometric KYC (country / ID type / ID number). What does it look like for Document Verification and Enhanced Document Verification — country plus document type, no ID number?
openQuestions.blocks: kycIdForm for the document products and Enhanced KYC
openQuestions.status: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-13 — RESOLVED: one identical form for every product needing details — Country, ID type, ID number — including both document products and Enhanced KYC. Simplest to build and test.

openQuestions.question: Product cards and profile avatars both use per-item colours (5 product hues, 3 profile hues observed). Which decorative token does each product and each profile get?
openQuestions.blocks: ProductCard and Avatar rendering identically across four platforms
openQuestions.status: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-13 — DECIDED: the designer supplies the mapping list once; stored in design-tokens.json. Still awaiting the list.

openQuestions.question: The products list shows 'SmartSelfie Authentication' in some frames and 'SmartSelfie Auth' in others (the grid uses 'SmartSelfie Auth'). Which string ships?
openQuestions.blocks: product labels and their derived test ids
openQuestions.status: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-13 — RESOLVED: 'SmartSelfie Authentication' everywhere, matching the SDK's job-type name. Note it wraps to two lines on the grid card.

openQuestions.question: Which element on the products screen opens the Switch profile sheet — the environment chip, or something else? The recording shows the sheet but not the trigger.
openQuestions.status: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-13 — RESOLVED: add a header AVATAR BUTTON next to the environment chip; it opens the sheet. The chip becomes display-only. Small design addition needed.

openQuestions.question: The scenario drawer is required by AGENTS.md and has test ids, but the design set has no frame for it. How should it present, and what opens it — a long-press on the header, a hidden gesture, or a row at the bottom of Settings?
openQuestions.blocks: the drawer's build only; every scenario is already reachable by launch argument
openQuestions.recommendation: A bottom sheet opened by a long-press on the environment chip, so it stays out of a partner's way while remaining reachable on a release build.
openQuestions.status: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-24 — RESOLVED: a 'Scenarios' row in a DEBUG section at the bottom of Settings, presented as a modal sheet, and the section is DEBUG-ONLY on every platform. Recorded as a deliberate addition: the design draws no DEBUG section, and this is the one place the app adds one. The earlier recommendation is withdrawn — the environment chip it hung off is now hidden (a token's api_url decides the environment), and a hidden long-press is undiscoverable to a partner reading the app. No launch argument reveals the row, deliberately: every device flow reaches the drawer by deep link (usesmileid-sample-android://debug/scenarios), so hiding it on release costs nothing testable, and a partner should never find a scenario picker in Settings on any build. This closes the last OPEN question in screens.json.

verifiedHow: Every board read with get_metadata: 8 sections, 39 frames, layer names, component instances and hotspot rectangles.
Two frames rendered and inspected visually (products grid 5206-4037, token-linked list 5206-2323), which corrected five component specs.

Navigation model inferred from named hotspot rectangles: every tab screen carries hotspot/tab-* to the other two tabs plus hotspot/token; verifications and the processing detail carry hotspot/pull-refresh; select mode hides the nav bar AND its hotspots and shows a selection bar instead.

notVerified.reason: Prototype reactions (the exact trigger→destination wiring) could not be read. The Plugin API route is blocked on this account — MCP edit tools require a Full Figma seat — and a prototype cannot be played from here.
edges: product card → next screen. No hotspot rectangle exists for the cards, so the destination may be a reaction on the card itself. The flow recorded in scenarios.json (products → [userDetails] → [KYC/ID form] → SDK flow) comes from the OWNER'S RULING of 2026-08-12, not from the prototype.
Settings PROFILE row → profiles / profileConfig (highly likely, unconfirmed).
scanToken entry point: which screens can reach it besides the token nav button.
Sheet dismissal behaviour (tap-scrim vs drag) for the four sheets.
notVerified.howToClose: Either grant a Full seat so the reaction graph can be read directly, or have someone play the prototype once and confirm the five edges above.

verification.finding: Board 01b — the CHOSEN products layout — carries no hotspot rectangles at all, while boards 01, 02, 06 and 07 do. The prototype therefore runs on the SUPERSEDED list layout, so playing it would demonstrate a screen we are not building. Worth telling the design team, and it means a play-through would not have validated the chosen products screen anyway.
